exposure: Israeli national oocyte donation law and its unique restrictions
sociodemographic characteristics of donors (age, marital status, child status, ethnicity)
sociodemographic characteristics of recipients (age, ethnicity, main indication for egg donation, use of donor/partner sperm)
outcome: Maternal complications (hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, gestational diabetes mellitus, caesarean sections)
cohort: The study included 26 financially compensated Jewish volunteer oocyte donors (mean age 29) and 69 Jewish recipients (mean age 44.6) who underwent IVF/embryo transfer cycles in one central IVF unit in Israel between March 2016 and November 2020.
finding: Pregnancy and live birth rates in the Israeli oocyte donation program were lower than published values in other programs, and the live birth rate was negatively associated with multiple embryo transfers.
mod_finding: A high caesarean section rate of 78.8% was observed among recipients.
